title: Default collation utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci causes inconsistent results to Korean

comments.text:
Hi Mr. rocky,

Thank you for your bug report.

However, this is not a bug.

The problem is in the default collation for the constants. Hence, you need to collate the constants to get consistent results. This is all described in our Reference Manual.

We have only changed a name of the database to "korean". We are sending you the entire output, one without a collation definition for each constant in the SELECT and the other one with a proper definition of the constants ..... Here are the results:

Hi, MySQL Verification Team.

Thank you for reply.

What I think is a bug is that
In Korean, '가나다' and 'ㄱㅏㄴㅏㄷㅏ' are strictly different strings due to the separation of graphemes, but utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci returns the result that these two strings are the same.

If I explicitly compare the collate of the constant
utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, it says the two strings are the same, (I think this is a bug)
utf8mb4_general_ci, it says they are different. (This is the correct result)

When comparing these two strings, they should be considered as different strings no matter what collation is used.
The utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci seems to have an error when comparing Korean characters, but is it normal because it is the intended result?

mysql> select '가나다' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci = 'ㄱㅏㄴㅏㄷㅏ' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, '가나다' collate utf8mb4_general_ci = 'ㄱㅏㄴㅏㄷㅏ' collate utf8mb4_general_ci;
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| '가나다' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci = 'ㄱㅏㄴㅏㄷㅏ' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci          | '가나다' collate utf8mb4_general_ci = 'ㄱㅏㄴㅏㄷㅏ' collate utf8mb4_general_ci          |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                                        1 |                                                                                        0 |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> select '달라요' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci = '달ㄹㅏㅇㅛ' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, '달라요' collate utf8mb4_general_ci = '달ㄹㅏㅇㅛ' collate utf8mb4_general_ci;
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| '달라요' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci = '달ㄹㅏㅇㅛ' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci         | '달라요' collate utf8mb4_general_ci = '달ㄹㅏㅇㅛ' collate utf8mb4_general_ci         |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                                     1 |                                                                                     0 |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

Hi,

You can observe that collating the constants changing the result.

You can try different COLLATE expressions.

Regarding Koreans language, we are not experts on this. 

We just implemented the UTF standard, to the last point.

Hence, you should contact the people that define Unicode standards.

Also, do not forget that two strings with different grapheme clusters can be considered identical, as per standard. There are many examples in the textbooks on this subject.

Not a bug.
